claims.claim: Crown Castle's June 30, 2026 tenant base is highly concentrated: its Form 10-Q reports approximately 93% of site-rental revenue for the first six months of 2026 came from T-Mobile, AT&T and Verizon Wireless. This makes carrier-specific capital allocation, consolidation or contract decisions a material cash-flow sensitivity even after the DISH exit is isolated.

The same filing reports a weighted-average remaining tenant-contract term of approximately five years and approximately $22.1 billion of expected future cash inflows excluding DISH amounts. Contract duration improves visibility, but it does not eliminate concentration risk because the cash-flow base is dominated by three counterparties.

risks.risk: Approximately 93% of first-half 2026 site-rental revenue came from three national carriers, creating concentrated exposure to their network spending and contract decisions.

contradictions.contradiction: Long-duration contracts and $22.1 billion of expected future cash inflows improve visibility while counterparty concentration remains structurally high.

unknowns.unknown: The degree to which future colocation and amendment growth can diversify economic dependence away from the three largest carriers remains unproven.

falsifiers: If future filings show a sustained decline in the top-three carrier revenue share while organic leasing remains healthy, the concentration-risk assessment should be reduced.

If renewal and amendment economics remain resilient through materially lower carrier capital spending, the inferred sensitivity of cash-flow growth to carrier concentration should be revised downward.
